memory_update.text: MOD is a high-priority second-order AI capex candidate for the cooling chokepoint because it has disclosed a customer-funded, multi-year, $4B data center cooling capacity agreement.

FIX maps to AI capex through mechanical/electrical and modular construction backlog rather than semiconductor exposure; key variable is whether technology/data-center backlog remains durable and high margin.

NVT should be tracked as a liquid-cooling and power/enclosure infrastructure supplier; exposure is plausible and supported by manufacturing expansion and NVIDIA-reference architecture involvement, but revenue mix requires verification.

CRDO is a connectivity chokepoint candidate for AI clusters through AECs and high-speed data-center networking; evidence is promising but needs primary-source validation for customer concentration and attach-rate durability.

APLD provides a more speculative but direct mapping to hyperscaler AI capacity through long-duration AI Factory leases; financing, construction, and power delivery risk are central falsification points.

Potential additional Layer 1B candidates not included due to five-name limit: DLR/EQIX for AI-ready data center REIT capacity, COHR/LITE/AAOI for optical transceivers, GLW for fiber/optical materials, and selected utilities/grid interconnection names.

node: Hyperscaler AI capex and cloud compute demand
summary: Expanded universe for the hyperscaler AI capex/cloud-demand node with emphasis on second-order and potentially underappreciated public-market mappings: cooling capacity, mechanical/electrical construction backlog, liquid-cooling/power enclosures, high-speed intra-cluster connectivity, and AI-ready colocation capacity. These names are not recommendations; they are research candidates whose exposure depends on continued hyperscaler capex, contracted capacity conversion, utilization, and AI workload ROI.
